steps: Prepare the existing fireplace
Confirm a clean, non-combustible chimney in good working order and block the damper fully open or remove it. Plan the gas line (left-side access) and power to the outlet box shown in Figure 2.1.

Approved for masonry and factory-built solid fuel burning fireplaces. Any part you remove must be capable of re-installation if the insert is ever removed (removing rivets or screws is acceptable).

  • Clean the chimney and fireplace to keep creosote odor out of the home. Verify combustible mantel and sidewall clearances (Section 8.1).
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and log grates may be removed. Smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if mechanically fastened, and firebrick to reach the minimum opening. Never cut sheet metal parts of the existing fireplace.
  • No gas access hole in a factory-built fireplace: drill one of 1½" or less through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox, and plug it with non-combustible insulation once the line is in.
  • The insert must not share or be connected to a chimney flue serving any other appliance.
  • Mechanically attach the warning label ("This fireplace has been converted for use with a gas fireplace insert only…") to the bottom of the existing firebox, where it stays visible if the insert is removed.
Measure & fit liners to the cap

Liner length is fireplace base to chimney top minus the insert height; cut the #816 flex to length. Fit the intake pipe over cap collar (A) and the exhaust pipe into high-temperature sealant on collar (B), (3) self-tapping screws each, and mark the exhaust end.

Measure (Section 3.4.1)

  1. Remove and discard the existing chimney cap.
  2. Measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney (two people make this easier).
  3. Subtract the height of the insert. The result is the length of co-linear flexible aluminum pipe needed.

Attach to the #816-CAP

  • #816: one roll of 35' of expandable 3" flexible pipe. #816-CAP: one round termination cap.
  • Combustion air intake pipe over intake collar (A); (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).
  • Bead of high temperature sealant around the base of exhaust collar (B); slide the exhaust pipe into it; (3) self-tapping screws (not provided). Mark the other end of the exhaust pipe.
  • The insert's exhaust flue collar is on the right side: install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right.
Run the liners down the chimney
Slide the vent adapter out of the channels on top of the insert. Feed both 3" x 3" pipes down the chimney, seal the cap to the chimney top and pull both pipes into the firebox.

• Offsets in the chimney: put a weighted rope around the pipe ends to guide them. Don't tie one rope around both pipes.
  • Recommended against cold air drafts: insulate the 3" x 3" flex pipes and chimney with unfaced insulation listed as non-combustible per ASTM E 136. Optional: wrap the first 3' below the cap before lowering, secured with wire.
  • Secure the cap with a liberal bead of sealant (not provided) around the top of the chimney.
  • Pull the exhaust pipe and combustion air intake down into the existing firebox. Avoid tight bends that can abrade or damage the flex pipe.
Connect liners to the vent adapter

Exhaust pipe inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', intake pipe over the intake collar: sealant and (3) ½" self-tapping screws each, then extra sealant around the joints. Each pipe must be on its correct collar at both the cap and the adapter.
Set, secure & level the insert

Slide the insert in until its top channels align with the adapter, then draw the adapter forward with the pull rod and latch tool until seated. Fix with (2) ½" sheet metal screws and level with the bolts (2 each side).
Gas line + leak check

Qualified person only (Massachusetts: licensed plumber or gas fitter); ½" tee handle manual shut-off and flexible connector to the ½" control valve inlet, routed through the left or back access clear of the fan. Check all connections with soapy water.

Install per local codes, or ANSI Z223.1 if there are none. The fireplace is manufactured for natural gas; convert with the kit first if it will run on propane.

  • The fireplace is equipped with a 3/8" x 18" long flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • A listed (and Massachusetts approved) ½" tee handle manual shut-off valve and flexible gas connector connect to the ½" control valve inlet. If substituting, check local codes.
  • Run the line preferably through the left gas line hole. The access hole cover (4 screws) can be repositioned for a left-side or back entry. Don't obstruct fan operation.
  • In a minimum-size opening, the gas line may need to be run after the insert is placed.
  • Supply-piping tests above ½ psi: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check every connection, field or factory made, with soapy water.
Panels, bulbs & log set
Convert to propane first if needed. Fit the refractory or black glass panels, then the ember bed light bulbs, then one of the required log sets per its own instructions.

• Access: remove the safety barrier, glass assembly, log set, crushed glass media and lava rock (if installed), the media tray/log rack (4 screws) and the light kit ((2) 7/16" nuts), then loosen (2) 7/16" nuts and remove the left and right burners.
  • Refractory NK34-CB900, NK34-L900, NK34-BB900, NK34-HB900: back panel into the lip at the back of the firebox; side panels slide up into place, front resting on the panel spacer, held by the 2 top clips bent to a 90° angle.
  • Black glass NK34-BG900: remove the bottom panel spacers (keep the 4 screws) and use the bottom panel clips from the kit, plus the top clips.
  • Front bottom light kit: (5) halogen bulbs from the components packet. Disconnect all electrical power first, and never touch halogen bulbs with bare hands.
  • A traditional or birch log set is required. Install the panels and all ember bed light bulbs before the logs.
Shroud & safety barrier
With the glass frame off, fix the shroud legs to the mounting nuts on each side with (4) Phillips truss head screws and refit the glass. Hang the barrier's tabs in the 4 slots on the glass frame.

• Trim panels or surrounds must not seal ventilation openings in the existing fireplace, and draft relief openings must not be covered or blocked.
  • Barrier: align the tabs on its back with the 4 slots on the glass frame (2 on each side), raise it slightly into the slots and let the tabs lower into position. To remove, lift up and out.
  • The barrier shall be installed. If it is damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this appliance (NK34-PSF, NK34A-MSF or NK34-RSF).
  • Outdoor covered installations: black painted barriers are highly recommended; plated or patina finishes are prone to oxidation and discoloration.
Initialize the controls

Rocker switch OFF, 4 AA in the backup holder, 3 AAA in the remote, then AC power; clear the firebox of packaging. Press the sync button (3 beeps, amber LED), then remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps, pilot lights), ON/OFF again, and set the rocker switch ON.

1. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF.
  2. Install (4) AA batteries (not included) in the backup battery holder and (3) AAA batteries (components packet) in the remote.
  3. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  4. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox. The next steps start the pilot in manual mode: the igniter sparks repeatedly and the pilot lights if gas is supplied.
  5. Lift off the safety barrier screen and press the remote sync button on the left side. 3 beeps and an amber LED mean the receiver is ready.
  6. Within 5 seconds, press ON/OFF on the remote. 4 beeps confirm the code, and the pilot lights. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out, confirming the command.
  7. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation and refit the barrier.
Pressure test & flame check

Read inlet pressure at the IN tap with all other gas appliances on and manifold pressure at the OUT tap, then re-seal each tap: turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose, tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten), relight and reattach the manometer; it should read no pressure. Flames start blue and turn yellow over the first 15 minutes; adjust venturis only in slight increments.

Inlet (IN tap) NG5" – 10.0" WC · 7" WC recommended
Inlet (IN tap) LP12" – 13" WC
Manifold (OUT tap) NG1.1" – 3.8" WC
Manifold (OUT tap) LP2.9" – 11" WC

Use a manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose. To re-seal each tap, turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose and tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.

Flame appearance

Venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician, with the fireplace cool; slight changes give dramatic results. Factory settings: NG 1/8" left and right, 5/8" rear; LP 5/16" left and right, 5/8" rear.

  • Dark orange flame with black tips: venturi closed too far, open slightly.
  • Short, blue flames, which may lift off the burner: venturi open too far, close slightly. The troubleshooting chart on p. 52 gives the same fix for a blue flame that lifts off the burner: close the air shutter slightly.
  • Lifting (ghosting) flames: gas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far. Check manometer settings and/or open the venturi slightly (p. 48).

panels.title: Pilot problems
items: Won't light: power interrupted → restore power or use the battery backup; wiring loose → check against the wiring schematic
Won't light: gas supply off → check every shut-off valve between appliance and main line
Won't stay lit: no propane or low gas pressure (bent line, narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult plumber or gas supplier
Won't stay lit: pilot adjustment screw not sealed, or pilot not enveloping the flame sensor
Won't go out: control set to CPI → set IPI

panels.title: Burner won't light / no response
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch to ON
Gas off, low supply, faulty wiring or plugged burner orifice
Pilot flame not directed to ignite the burner
Remote or backup batteries low → replace; no remote–IFC link → reprogram the remote
Maximum failed ignitions reached → reset the IFC module; no call for heat → remote ON, thermostat OFF

panels.title: Goes out while running
items: Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked
Exhaust vent pipe leaking exhaust back into the firebox

panels.title: Soot or lifting flames
items: Soot on glass: improper log placement → see Section 9.4
Soot on glass: venturi settings → open the air shutters slightly
Blue flame lifting off burner: venturi setting → close the air shutter slightly
Either: vent cap installed wrong, blocked, or vent system leaking → adjust, clear or repair

codes: Below 4V; IFC double-beeps on ON/OFF and ignores commands until batteries are replaced
Two failed ignition tries; verify gas is on and sensor not shorted, then re-initialize (Section 11.2)

light.title: Turning it on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights electronically. The remote starts it, and the control sparks a pilot flame that lights the burner.

Turn it on

  1. The main ON/OFF rocker switch must be ON. It's on the left side of the unit, behind the safety barrier screen.
  2. With the fireplace off, press ON/OFF on the remote. You'll hear one beep, and the remote screen shows all active icons.
  3. About 4 seconds later the control starts sparking at the pilot.

If it doesn't light

The control tries twice. Each try sparks for about 60 seconds, with a pause of about 35 seconds between. If both fail, it locks out, and a red light on the control blinks 3 times, over and over. Check that the gas is turned on. To reset, press ON/OFF on the remote, wait about 2 seconds and press it again. The rocker switch works the same way: OFF, wait 2 seconds, ON.

Turn it off

Press ON/OFF while it's running. You'll hear one beep, the burner goes out, and the screen shows only the room temperature. If the pilot is set to continuous (CPI), the pilot stays lit.

A red light blinking 2 times means a pilot flame error. Contact your dealer.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote controls the burner, flame height, thermostat, fan and lights. The fireplace answers most commands with a single beep.

Flame height

There are 6 flame levels. Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one level, all the way to off. The up arrow raises it one step. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, pressing up relights it on HI.

Thermostat

Press the thermostat key to show the room and set temperatures, then use the arrows to pick your setting. Keep pressing it until SMART appears for smart mode, which turns the flame down as the room reaches your setting. In smart mode you can't change the flame height by hand.

Handy extras

  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together to lock or unlock the keys. A lock icon shows while locked.
  • °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press the thermostat and Mode keys together.

Running it without the remote

Lift off the safety barrier screen and set the rocker switch OFF. Hold the remote sync button until it beeps 3 times and an amber light comes on, then press it again within 5 seconds. The pilot lights, and the rocker switch now turns the burner on (HI only) and off.

sounds.title: Beeps, blinks and noises
sounds.html:
The control module answers you with beeps and a small light.

1 beepCommand received
Double-beep when you press ON/OFFBackup batteries low
3 beeps and an amber lightReady to pair with the remote
4 beepsRemote paired

A blinking red light

  • 1 blink, repeating: the backup batteries are low. Replace them.
  • 2 blinks: pilot flame error. Contact your dealer.
  • 3 blinks: it locked out after two failed tries to light. Check that the gas is on, then reset it (see "Turn it on and off").

It switched off for a few seconds?

When the pilot has stayed lit, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to run a safety check. Then it goes back to your last command.

Ticks and creaks

Some minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts that makes noise is normal and not a defect.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is the yearly job the manual gives you, the homeowner.

  1. Let the fireplace cool completely. Never remove or clean the glass while it's hot.
  2. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  3. Lift the safety barrier screen up and out of its slots.
  4. With the glass latch tool from the components packet, pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom out and up. Lift the glass up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  5. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  6. Hang the glass back on the top tabs, lower the bottom into place, and pull the latches out and down over their tabs. Put the safety screen back.
Don't run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or without the safety screen. Don't strike or slam the glass, and wear protective gloves to handle broken glass.

Damaged glass is replaced as a complete assembly (part 700-032T), supplied only by Hussong Mfg., by a qualified service person.

The manual also prints the glass assembly as #701-032T (p. 54); its parts list gives 700-032T, Glass with Gasket - 21-1/2" x 29-7/8" (p. 56).

flame.title: How the flame should look
flame.html:
When the fireplace is first lit, the burner flames look blue. During the first 15 minutes of operation they gradually turn the yellow color they're meant to have.

A good flame burns steady. It shouldn't lift or float off the burner.

When to call a technician

  • The flames stay blue.
  • They turn dark orange with black tips, or soot builds up on the glass.
  • They lift off the burner.

The burner's air shutters (venturis) may need adjusting. That must be done by a qualified service technician. Soot on the glass can also come from logs that aren't placed correctly, or from a problem at the vent cap.

Flame appearance also depends on altitude, fuel quality and the vent setup, so a new installation may need some fine-tuning.

modes.title: Pilot settings: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
The pilot is the flame that lights the burner. Your fireplace has two pilot settings.

  • IPI (intermittent pilot): the control sparks the pilot each time you turn the fireplace on.
  • CPI (continuous pilot): the pilot stays lit. This keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less airflow disruption.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the remote screen means CPI. No snowflake means IPI.

To switch

  1. Turn the fireplace off with the remote.
  2. Press Mode until the CPI icon is selected.
  3. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow for IPI. One beep confirms.

The 7-day timeout

In CPI, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. That's a standard safety feature. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.

If the pilot won't go out, the system is set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

fan.title: Fan and lights
fan.html:
Fan

The fan has 6 speeds. Press Mode until the fan icon is selected, then use the up and down arrows to turn it on, off or change speed.

  • Thermostat mode: the fan waits 5 minutes after the fireplace lights, so heat can build first. It keeps running about 12 minutes after the fireplace turns off.
  • Manual mode: the fan runs at its last setting, with no delay starting or stopping.

Top accent light

It has 6 brightness levels. Press Mode to the light icon, then use the arrows.

Ember bed light

Press Mode to the AUX icon. The up arrow turns it on and the down arrow turns it off. To change its brightness, lift off the safety barrier screen and turn the knob on the left side of the firebox: clockwise for brighter, counterclockwise for dimmer. Put the screen back when you're done.

The fan and lights don't work on backup battery power during an outage.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120VAC house power, with a battery backup so you can still use it in a power outage.

Backup battery holder (control module)4 × AA (not included)
Remote control3 × AAA (included)

During an outage

The 6 volt backup battery pack keeps the burner and flame height adjustment working. The fan and accent light won't work until power comes back.

Low batteries

  • Backup pack: the control double-beeps when you press ON/OFF, and the red light blinks once at intervals. It won't take commands until you replace the batteries. It beeps once when it powers back up.
  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen before the power runs out. It goes away once you put in new batteries.

Battery life depends on battery quality, how often the fireplace lights and, for the remote, how often you change the thermostat setting.

safety.title: Safety and yearly service
safety.html:
• The viewing glass gets hot. The safety barrier screen that comes with the fireplace reduces the risk of burns, and it must be installed to protect children and other at-risk people.
  • Never run the fireplace without the safety screen, or with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • If the barrier gets damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace.
  • Its surfaces get very hot, so it should sit out of traffic and away from furniture and drapes.
  • Keep the area around it clear of anything that burns, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use the fireplace. Call a qualified service technician right away.

Yearly service

Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a professional service person. They clean and check the firebox, fan, vent system, burner and pilot. Lots of lint from carpeting or bedding can mean it needs cleaning more often.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants your Kozy Heat fireplace to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship.

30 days · parts & laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborAll parts and material except the 30-day items
Years 2 through lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. Registering needs no paperwork sent in: keep your proof of purchase, with the serial number and model, for any claim. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual.
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the fireplace altered or tampered with.
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation.
  • It isn't transferable, and it doesn't cover normal wear and tear or how well it heats your space.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5" WC min · 7" WC recommended · 10" WC max
Propane12" WC min · 13" WC max

Measure at the valve's IN tap (A) with all other gas appliances in the house on, or at full capacity: loosen the tap screw, attach a manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose, light pilot and burner, read. Then re-seal the tap: turn off burner and pilot, disconnect the hose, tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to tap A to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure. If inlet pressure is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust it.

Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve from the supply piping for test pressures above ½ psi; at ½ psi or less, close its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas low / high1.1" / 3.8" WC
Propane low / high2.9" / 11" WC

Measure at the OUT tap (B): light the pilot, loosen the tap, attach a manometer (1/4" I.D. hose), light the burner and compare with Table 12.2. Turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the manometer hose and re-tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten). Then attach the manometer to tap B to verify it's completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Valve: S.I.T. IPI gas valve (NG 700-567, LP 700-567-1) with valve stepper motor, 50% turndown (NG 700-504, LP 700-504-1).

specVent.title: Chimney & liner venting
specVent.html:
Existing chimney, min. inside diameter6" x 8" masonry · 7" factory-built solid fuel (Class A metal)
Existing chimney height10' min · 40' max
Liner3" x 3" co-linear flex (Kozy Heat #816: 35' roll)
Max horizontal run, 3" x 3" flex24"
Co-linear + co-axial combined10' min · 40' max (NG and LP)
Vent cap to intersecting walls, overhangs, eaves12"

Never share a flue with another appliance. The exhaust collar is on the right; install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right too. Approved 3" x 3" co-linear caps (Table 6.1): Ameri-Vent DVCC33; BDM 940033HWS, 940033; Simpson DuraVent 46DVA-CL33H, 46DVA-CL33P; ICC CT3, IVT; Kozy Heat 816-CAP; Metal Fab 4DVT33F; Olympia VDV-RCL33. Minimum cap height above a flat to 6/12 roof is 1.0 ft; steeper pitches are in the table on p. 15.

Where the chimney no longer reaches the roofline, an approved 4" x 6-5/8" co-linear to co-axial adapter may be installed where it ends; the co-axial pipe after it needs 1" clearance to combustibles on all sides. Approved co-axial caps: Table 6.4 (p. 20).

Note: pp. 19 and 20 say maximum horizontal vent runs of 24" require a 1" rise per 12" of run; the troubleshooting chart on p. 51 says a 1/4" rise for every 12" of travel is required on horizontal venting.

Either mantel can gain 1" of depth for every 1" of added height (Figure 8.4). The hearth may be combustible; the front of the fireplace and the hearth must be flush, or the hearth below the fireplace floor. For the safety barrier to install properly, the bottom of the fireplace must be level with the finished hearth (p. 11). Keep service access clearances.

Outdoor covered installation (Section 6.8): operation approved from 40°F to 110°F; the overhang depth, and its width to each side, must be at least 1/2 of the roofline elevation above the fireplace base.

Glass assembly part number: #701-032T in the maintenance section (p. 54) vs 700-032T 'Glass with Gasket - 21-1/2" x 29-7/8"' in the parts list (p. 56).

Remedy for lifting flames: Table 12.4 (p. 48) blames lifting (ghosting) flames on gas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far and says open the venturi slightly; the troubleshooting chart (p. 52) says a blue flame that lifts off the burner needs the air shutter closed slightly, and p. 48's own text says opening the shutter gives a short blue flame that may lift.
conflicts.reason: Two different flames: p. 48's text and Table 12.4 tie a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner to the venturi open too far (close it slightly), the same fix p. 52 gives for a blue flame that lifts off the burner; Table 12.4's separate row for lifting (ghosting) flames gives gas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far (check manometer settings and/or open slightly).

catalog_mismatches.manual: a non-combustible mantel of max 8" (203mm) depth needs a minimum vertical clearance of 1" (25mm) above the top of the appliance

review.notes: No text on pp. 2, 4, 6 (blank or image-only) or on p. 39 (the 11.0 Operating Instructions page, probably the lighting/safety label as a graphic), so the text has no 'if you smell gas' or lighting-label wording and the guide has no gas-smell drawer. Figure-only content not transcribed: appliance dimensions (Fig. 2.1, p. 9), safety barrier dimensions (p. 11), floor clearance (Fig. 3.1, p. 12), co-linear/co-axial termination clearances (Figs. 4.2-4.3 and Table 4.1, p. 16), outdoor covered drawings (pp. 24-25), mantel/hearth figures (pp. 28-29), wiring diagrams (pp. 36-38), correct flame appearance (Fig. 14.3, p. 54). The roof-pitch table on p. 15 lost its pitch labels except 'Flat to 6/12' (1.0 ft); only that row is used. The manual text gives no efficiency, overall insert dimensions or view area, so catalog efficiency, height/width/depth and view_area were not checked; catalog height 23.75 and depth 16.375 equal the minimum opening height and depth on p. 13, not necessarily the insert size. Catalog feature 'one-piece shroud required' is not stated in the manual, which lists 4-piece and 1-piece shrouds (p. 56). p. 26 says the fireplace is equipped with a 3/8" x 18" flexible gas connector; the parts list (p. 55) shows a 24" Flex Gas Line 700-224B and a 24" Black 3/8" Gas Line 700-382B, relation unclear. Hearth: p. 27 allows the hearth flush with or below the fireplace floor, while p. 11 says the barrier needs the fireplace bottom level with the finished hearth; both are shown in specClear. Minor: p. 18 cites 'Section 3.2.2' for chimney specs (they are in 3.4, p. 14); the TOC calls 11.4 'Automatic Safety Restart' but the page says 'Automatic Safety Turn-off'; p. 22 says exhaust-collar screws are not provided but intake-collar screws are provided; max horizontal flex run is printed 24" (609mm) on p. 19 and 24" (610mm) on p. 20 (inch value used). Massachusetts requirements (p. 7) address sidewall-vented equipment and were not carried into the guide.
